title: Funnel neckline shirt
content:
"This is my second post as a CONNECT supporter for CLO SET CONNECT! In this video, I showcase my workflow for creating a cotton jersey shirt with a funnel neckline in CLO 3D. I used tools like 'Pen on Garment' and 'Pen on Avatar' to shape and refine the design directly in 3D. Watch the full process on YouTube and discover new techniques to enhance your creations!"

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/389be5752da449e29919500a0f4ada49/images/162d14936da745159240bd6a3936ecb5doll_56.png)

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta-_Y8Py_s4

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Your tutorial is fantastic! The approach is straightforward, and it's an excellent guide that's easy to understand. I think many users will find your tutorial helpful and will benefit from it. Thank you for sharing!💞
Reply 1: So sweet thank you. your comments encourage me to make more and more tutorials.

Comment 2: That’s seriously cool! Wish I could do this, but I can’t. Because I, with my years of training as a patterns cutter and then working as a bespoke tailor, am simply unable to create garments using Pen tool. First, because for me there must be a technical basis to build a garment upon. What I mean is a “basic, professionally drafted pattern”. Second, because I view Clo3D as a pattern prototyping tool rather than a 3D garment creating app. And last, but not least: because I always consider real life’s practical and comfort aspects of the garments I design.Would you consider using for your amazing creations one of the patterns I sell? I would provide it free of charge. And I would be honoured.

Your job is valuable and that is what i always say to the fashion students," perfect visual does not mean perfect fit "so i encourage them to learn at least the essential basic knowledge of drawing patterns and therefore CLO has efficient tools in 2d window.I appreciate your offer and i will keep it in my mind and again thanks for your time and comment.

title: Cloth sticking to body
content:
Actually I'm trying to model saree in marvelous designer . 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/53c4cdfa55d04d9e9fd4d0f072d78258/images/f3a6e250e77046c39b87e195592c8f39inbound7287718712040111141.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/53c4cdfa55d04d9e9fd4d0f072d78258/images/d17f30e16626471bb37bd7c7600768dainbound941643131468117558.png)

So the issue is this, no matter what I change this issue is not solving . I tried to add pressure but the whole piece of cloth is moving to a side instead of staying straight. It will be helpful if any one comes up with any solution.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/53c4cdfa55d04d9e9fd4d0f072d78258/images/7a5bb8272aa64b67833c9be069689525inbound3868176707357801476.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/53c4cdfa55d04d9e9fd4d0f072d78258/images/1d2ac7246efc40f19e820ba1601925b4inbound166494935617952604.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/53c4cdfa55d04d9e9fd4d0f072d78258/images/f05b73b0c57a4373a57c4f4a10ca7eb2inbound3112064500234105972.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Pressure is a value that affects the force exerted by the garments in the direction of their normals. This means that they will move where they have a greater force. If the patterns you use are symmetrical, the force will be equal on both parts and a swelling effect will be generated. If one of the patterns is uneven and has a greater proportion than the other pattern that exerts a reverse pressure force, the total force of this larger pattern will be the one that predominates since its effect space can be an unbalancing factor and therefore an imbalance to one side.If you want to keep the patterns more firmly, you can always use different Fabrics to get as close to your goal as possible and then work with the property values.
content_description: This page seeks advice and solutions for stabilizing and accurately modeling a saree garment in Marvelous Designer to prevent unwanted cloth movement.

title: Making textures
content:
Hello, I have made some clothes in Marvelous designer. I want to make textures in other software like Substance painter or Photoshop. So is it possible to import those textures back in Marvelous designer to apply on clothes and export it as zprj format? If yes pls explain the procedure. Thank you.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Yes, you just need to export the maps from the software you are going to use for texturing. Using the PBR format.Then use the different maps (Albedo, Roughness, Metallicity, Transparency, Normal...) in their respective place in the Fabric Properties tab.This way you can use the texture from any other third-party software for texturing.
Reply 1: Thank you
content_description: This web page aims to explain how to create textures in external software like Substance Painter or Photoshop and import them back into Marvelous Designer to apply on clothes and export the project in zprj format.

title: Fabric preset settings
content:
Can anyone share more detailed info about the fabric preset settings in marvelous designer.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Sure! You have different options distributed by types of real-life fabrics. If you are looking for more specific behavior, you can always use a default fabric and adjust the parameters.If you are new to Marvelous Designer, I would recommend using the Default_For_Simulation and getting used to the different tools in the software.Once you want to achieve a desired garment, you should research the fabric used in real life for its production and use one of the options from our default set.If you are looking for a fabric with more solid behavior, you can try Trim_Fusible_Rigid, Trim_Hardware, or Trim_Full_Grain_Leather. It will obviously depend on the objective, but they surely have base parameters that can serve as a good starting point.If you need more info, let me know!
content_description: This page serves to gather and share detailed information about fabric preset settings in Marvelous Designer.
